content.text:
Chamber C's etch rate stepped up after preventive maintenance PM-C-1126 (edge ring replaced, chamber wet clean, ended 01:40 UTC on 27 Nov), and the eight lots run since then are on hold with edge-ring failures found at sort.

**What the FDC shows (ETCH-C, as of 07:45 UTC):**
- Runs 1 to 22 (26 Nov) held between 49.2 and 51.1 nm/min, centre 50.0, limits 47.0 and 53.0.
- From run 23 (lot N2-0811, 51.9 nm/min) every run after the PM ran high: 51.9 to 53.8 nm/min.
- Run 25 (53.6) and run 30 (53.8) broke the upper limit (rule 1). Run 27 tripped rule 2, two of three runs beyond two sigma. The ETCH_RATE_HIGH alarm opened at 02:14.

**What is exposed:** lots N2-0811 to N2-0818, 200 wafers, all on hold per MES. The sort test found edge-ring failures on 5 of the 8 sampled lots (N2-0813, N2-0815, N2-0816, N2-0817, N2-0818). The other three sampled lots passed.

**What the engineer would decide:**
- Keep all eight lots on hold. Five of eight sampled lots failing at the edge ring points to the post-PM chamber state, not a random lot.
- Look at the edge-ring install and chamber C's post-PM qualification before any run is released.
- Decide on disposition for the eight lots once the sort and chamber findings are reviewed. I can't release or change holds; that is signed in the MES.

Times are UTC as the tool reports them.

Chamber C's etch rate shifted high right after the PM-C-1126 maintenance and has stayed high. The sort test now shows edge-ring failures on the lots it has run since.

- **Before the PM:** Runs 1–22 were stable at 49.2–51.1 nm/min, centred on 50.0.

- **Alarms:**
  - FDC opened ETCH_RATE_HIGH at 02:14, on run 24 at 52.4.

- **Product impact:**
  - Eight lots ran after the PM, N2-0811 to N2-0818, which is 200 wafers. All eight are on hold.
  - At sort (06:20), 5 of the 8 sampled wafers show edge-ring failures. The failing lots are N2-0813, N2-0815, N2-0816, N2-0817 and N2-0818.
  - N2-0811, N2-0812 and N2-0814 sampled clean. One sampled wafer per lot is a thin basis for clearing them.

**What the data suggests**
The onset coincides exactly with the PM, and the failures are at the edge, where the ring was replaced. That points to the edge-ring install or seating, or to chamber conditioning after the wet clean. This is a correlation, because I can't see the cause in the data.

**Next steps for an engineer to sign off**
- Keep chamber C out of production until the edge ring and its seating are checked. Consider re-qualifying it with a conditioning run or a monitor wafer.
- Keep all eight lots on hold. Don't release the three clean-sampling lots on one wafer each. Instead, sample more wafers from them or use the per-wafer edge-zone data.
